title: Φωτογραφίζω με το κινητό

event.venue: Εργαστήρι Ακτίδα — επινοημένος χώρος χωρίς πραγματική διεύθυνση
event.staff: One lead instructor and three practice tutors; all fictional and unnamed.
event.equipment: Participants use their own smartphones and built-in camera/editing tools. No paid app, account creation or public image upload is required.

schedule.activity: Live demonstration: focus, exposure adjustment and framing
Rotation 1: G01–G05 light practice in courtyard; G06–G10 composition practice in hall
Rotation 2: G06–G10 light practice in courtyard; G01–G05 composition practice in hall
Built-in editing: crop, straighten, brightness and a before/after comparison
Voluntary image critique; twelve images discussed
Recap and announcement of next-day handout

exercises.task: Photograph the same tabletop object in direct and shaded daylight; adjust exposure and compare the pair.
exercises.constraint: No portrait or identifiable-person photography is required.

exercises.task: Make three frames of a simple still life from different positions, then compare subject placement with a partner.
exercises.constraint: All ten people remain in their assigned practice group; each works with a partner or small subset.

exercises.task: Crop, straighten and adjust brightness on one of your own practice photos using the phone's built-in editor.
exercises.constraint: This is introductory editing, with no advanced retouching segment.

observations.occurrence: The lead instructor showed the same scene before and after changing exposure and repeated the adjustment once.
observations.eligibleWitnesses: Attendees present during the opening demonstration.
possibleImpressions: The example finally made exposure understandable.
The demonstration repeated something already familiar.
Watching was easier than finding the control later.

observations.occurrence: The workshop admitted adults without a skill prerequisite and used mixed-experience practice groups; no beginner/advanced tracks were offered.
observations.eligibleWitnesses: Participants know their own skill and the exchanges they personally witnessed, not the skill distribution of all 100 people.
possibleImpressions: The beginner pace suited me.
Some steps moved too quickly for me.
I wanted a separate advanced group.

observations.occurrence: The main microphone briefly cut out twice between 14:25 and 14:35; the instructor continued speaking while it was restored.
observations.eligibleWitnesses: Attendees present then; missed-word complaints apply particularly to rear seats. Front seats may have heard adequately.
possibleImpressions: I missed part of the explanation at the back.
It was a brief interruption without much impact.

observations.occurrence: Daylight from the right-hand windows reduced projected-screen contrast for right-side seats during the opening demonstration.
observations.eligibleWitnesses: Right-side demonstration attendees; an assigned move or firsthand observation is needed for anyone elsewhere to describe the view.
possibleImpressions: Small menu labels were hard to see.
The spoken explanation was enough despite the glare.

observations.occurrence: Passing rain paused the second courtyard rotation from 15:55 to 16:05. G06–G10 sheltered in the covered side gallery; the session still ended at 16:20, leaving 25 rather than 35 usable practice minutes. The indoor rotation continued.
observations.eligibleWitnesses: G06–G10 members present for the second rotation experienced this directly. Other groups cannot claim their own exercise lost those ten minutes.
possibleImpressions: I needed more time to compare my light shots.
I finished the pair despite the shorter session.
The move to shelter was handled calmly.

observations.occurrence: Each group had a 35-minute indoor composition slot with movable still-life objects and a partner comparison.
observations.eligibleWitnesses: People present for their own indoor rotation.
possibleImpressions: Changing position improved my framing.
The still-life setup felt repetitive.
I preferred the indoor exercise to the light exercise.

observations.occurrence: A practice tutor visited G01 and G03 during the first courtyard rotation and G06 and G08 during the second, giving brief individual exposure-control help to participants who asked.
observations.eligibleWitnesses: Members of those groups present for the visit; only profiles assigned direct help may claim they received it.
possibleImpressions: The personal explanation solved my problem.
The visit helped a partner more than me.
The help was useful but brief.

observations.occurrence: Participants in G04 and G09 who requested courtyard help waited while the tutors were with other groups; some continued with a partner before a tutor became available.
observations.eligibleWitnesses: G04/G09 participants assigned a help request or a witnessed wait in their profiles.
possibleImpressions: The wait used up practice time.
A partner helped while I waited.
The delay was manageable.

observations.occurrence: The demonstration phone was an iPhone. Some Android camera apps placed exposure controls behind different icons or gestures; the basic exercise still worked on those phones.
observations.eligibleWitnesses: Assigned Android participants who looked for the controls, or profiles explicitly witnessing a partner's difficulty. This does not affect every Android phone.
possibleImpressions: I lost time finding the matching menu.
A short Android example would have helped.
I found the equivalent control without trouble.

observations.occurrence: More than twelve images were volunteered for the closing critique, but time allowed discussion of twelve. There was no promise that every attendee's image would be reviewed.
observations.eligibleWitnesses: Attendees present from 17:10; only assigned submitters may say their own image was not reached.
possibleImpressions: I wanted feedback on my own photo.
Listening to other critiques was useful.
The final section felt long.

observations.occurrence: At the 17:45 recap the organizer promised a short recap handout by 12:00 the next day. At the 18:30 feedback invitation it had not been sent and was not overdue.
observations.eligibleWitnesses: Attendees present for the recap, or profiles explicitly told about it by someone else.
possibleImpressions: I look forward to the handout.
I would have preferred a sheet during practice.
I am unsure where it will arrive.

observations.occurrence: Courtyard practice was primarily standing around worktables. Chairs were available inside the hall, with no chair placed at each courtyard table.
observations.eligibleWitnesses: People who attended courtyard practice; only assigned personal testimony supports fatigue or discomfort.
possibleImpressions: Standing became tiring for me.
I wanted somewhere to sit during the outdoor task.
The standing arrangement was fine for me.

observations.occurrence: Exercises included optional partner comparison within each ten-person group; strangers sometimes exchanged tips while practicing.
observations.eligibleWitnesses: Only the exchanges assigned to an individual profile; no participant can infer that every group was friendly.
possibleImpressions: A partner's tip was useful.
Comparing shots made the exercise enjoyable.
I preferred to work quietly.

observations.occurrence: The 35-minute editing segment covered crop, straighten and brightness with one before/after comparison.
possibleImpressions: The editing was too basic for my experience.
Those basic controls were exactly what I needed.
I would rather have spent some of this time practicing light.

participantKnowledgeRules: The event brief is author knowledge, not a participant's script. A profile narrows which facts a person experienced and which opinions they hold.
An observation ID is an authoring reference, not an extraction category, required mention or finding.
Do not give a participant knowledge of other groups, missed sessions, staff intentions or other people's feelings without explicit hearsay in the profile.
Keep hearsay and uncertainty qualified. A subjective complaint is not proof of an event-wide failure.
A witness can be neutral about an incident; an assigned fact does not require testimony about it.
Silent participants provide no testimony. Partial conversations leave unanswered matters unknown.
Do not add real identities, phone numbers, addresses, accounts or links. All people and event details are fictional.

proposedInterviewContract.purpose: Gather a short overall impression and, only if useful, clarify one relevant point in the participant's own feedback.
proposedInterviewContract.status: Authored transcript fixture contract only; does not implement or adapt the application's existing V2 questionnaire.
proposedInterviewContract.opening: Γεια σου! Πώς σου φάνηκε συνολικά το σημερινό εργαστήριο φωτογραφίας με κινητό; Αν θέλεις, πες μας με λίγα λόγια.
proposedInterviewContract.followUpRule: Ask at most one short, open, non-leading clarification when the answer leaves useful context missing. Reflect only what the person actually said; do not supply incident names or suspected causes. Skip the follow-up when the feedback is already clear, the participant declines, or the participant stops responding.
proposedInterviewContract.exampleClarification: Σε ποιο μέρος του εργαστηρίου αναφέρεσαι;
proposedInterviewContract.completion: Thank the participant briefly when they finish; do not require ratings, attendance intentions or answers about every exercise.
proposedInterviewContract.declineAndStop: Respect any explicit refusal or STOP immediately. A brief acknowledgment is allowed; no further question, persuasion or reminder.
proposedInterviewContract.silence: An unanswered opening has no participant messages. An unanswered follow-up remains partial, without an invented reply or claim of completion.
proposedInterviewContract.scheduling: Conversation timestamps, if used, begin at or after the fictional 18:30 invitation. Next-day delivery failure cannot be inferred from same-evening testimony.
